subject: Operational plan for no-adaptive-learning commitments, subprocessor evidence, and per-route controls
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@medanalytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@csp-integrations.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: No-adaptive-learning commitments + evidence for procurement

Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has two gating items before we can move to an LOI: (1) an explicit no-adaptive-learning commitment for our tenant data (we can accept telemetry/metrics but no training on raw prompts/responses), and (2) an evidence pack that shows which subprocessors touch data in the inference path and how you prove no-training (attestations, KMS residency, audit logs).

Specifically, our security team asked:
- Can you commit to a per-customer/no-training toggle (route-level) that prevents model updates from any captured interaction?
- What operational evidence do you provide to show model improvement pipelines are isolated (e.g., KV cache retention, ephemeral prompt logs, export controls, and deletion timelines)?
- We also need a subprocessor inventory plus a simple description of what each subprocessor does with regard to transient storage vs persistence.

Can you send a short ops playbook and a redline of your DPA that includes the above? We need to present to legal and InfoSec on Thursday.

Thanks,
Claire
VP, Security & Compliance
MedAnalytics
(attachment: procurement_requirements_20261101.pdf)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@csp-integrations.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-adaptive-learning commitments + evidence for procurement

Claire —

Appreciate the clarity and the timeline. We can meet the gating items; below is what I'll send in one consolidated package for your review by EOD Wednesday:

1) Operational controls summary (how per-route/no-train toggles are implemented at the routing layer, and how they are enforced end-to-end).
2) Evidence pack: a) current subprocessor inventory (roles + data paths), b) sample attestation doc for our training pipelines, c) audit log snippets showing no-transfer to training buckets for a demo tenant.
3) DPA redline capturing the no-adaptive-learning clause and the per-route operational SOW language.

Quick notes:
- We support per-route \"no-train\" flags that are enforced as request tags at the gateway; requests with that tag are routed to ephemeral inference-only paths with a strict TTL on caches and no export to model training queues.
- Telemetry (aggregated token counts, error rates) can be retained for service health; raw prompt/response payloads are never sent to training without explicit opt-in.
- We will provide a subprocessor spreadsheet showing where transient storage exists vs persistent storage.

Looping in Neha for legal redlines and David for the ops evidence. Tom — feel free to add any integration specifics for your SFTP/onboarding flow.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachments to follow: MedAnalytics_DPA_redline_20261102.pdf)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medanalytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@csp-integrations.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-adaptive-learning commitments + evidence for procurement

Claire / Aditya —

Attached is a redline of the DPA with the proposed no-adaptive-learning clause and a short SOW paragraph that maps the per-route toggle to operational responsibilities. High level: we accept a no-training commitment scoped to tenant-derived prompts/responses (Section 4.2), with exceptions for aggregated telemetry defined in Section 6. We added explicit definitions for \"training\" and \"telemetry\" to avoid ambiguity.

I also attached a subprocessor inventory (v1). Notes:
- We call out the inference stack subprocessors (cache layer provider, metrics pipeline, object store) and indicate which components see ephemeral vs persistent data.
- We can provide signed attestations from our training infra team showing that data tagged with the no-train flag is excluded from model update pipelines; the attestation will include a pointer to the audit log excerpts.

Next steps for MedAnalytics review:
- Legal: confirm the scope language matches what you need (tenant data only).
- InfoSec: we can schedule a short tech-runthrough with David to show the live routing and the audit proof.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
(attachments: MedAnalytics_DPA_redline_20261102.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20261103.xlsx)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medanalytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@csp-integrations.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-adaptive-learning commitments + evidence for procurement

Claire —

Happy to run the tech session. What I'll demo in 20 minutes:
- How we set the per-route no-train flag at the gateway (trace of request headers and internal routing decisions).
- The ephemeral inference path (cache TTLs set to <5 minutes for no-train routes), and the immutability of export rules (no export rule exists for traffic with that tag).
- Audit log snippet showing a sample request from \"medanalytics-demo\" and the absence of any export to training buckets (I will present the log excerpt and hashed identifiers rather than PII).
- Subprocessor callouts where transient storage exists (we mark the object store ephemeral mount and the metrics pipeline as aggregated-only).

Proposed times: Friday 10:00–10:30 PT or Monday 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works for your team?

Also attaching the two files Neha referenced for convenience.

—David
David Kim
Head of Platform Security — Redwood Inference
(attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20261103.xlsx, MedAnalytics_DPA_redline_20261102.pdf)
